q.t: A seed turning into a sprout is called…
q.e: Germination is the start of a new plant.

q.t: Anything that prompts a living being to respond is a…
q.e: A thorn or a hot cup are stimuli.

q.t: Producing new ones of one's own kind is…
q.e: It is necessary for the continuity of life.

q.t: Plants take air in and out through…
q.e: Tiny pores on leaves.

q.t: Touch-me-not (chhui-mui) folding its leaves shows…
q.e: Touch is the stimulus; folding is the response.

q.t: Sweat is a form of…
q.e: It removes water and salts.

q.t: Drosera is a plant that…
q.e: It is insectivorous, using sticky hairs.

q.t: Which is non-living even though it moves?
q.e: It can't grow, reproduce, respire or respond.

q.t: Which TWO are essential for germination?
q.e: Sunlight is not essential for most seeds.

q.t: The tiny plant inside a seed is the…
q.e: Water helps the embryo develop.

q.t: Why is movement alone not proof of life?
o: Non-living things like cars also move
q.e: The test is the whole set of characteristics.

q.t: Why are plants living though they don't walk?
o: They show all other characteristics, and parts move
q.e: Flowers open, climbers wind around supports.

q.t: Plants excrete excess water and minerals as…
q.e: Seen on grasses and roses.

q.t: Amla leaves closing after sunset show…
q.e: Darkness is the stimulus.

q.t: Pot A (sunlight, no water) seeds don't germinate because…
o: Water is needed to soften the seed coat
q.e: Without water, the embryo can't develop.

q.t: Pot C (moist soil, dark) seeds germinate. This shows…
q.e: Most seeds don't need light to germinate.

q.t: After germination, the seedling needs sunlight to…
q.e: Light is needed for further growth.

q.t: A living being is called dead when…
o: It can't show life characteristics despite having resources
q.e: Even with food, air and water, it shows no life processes.

q.t: A child outgrowing old clothes shows…
q.e: Growth is a characteristic of living things.

q.t: Climbers winding round supports show plants can…
q.e: Plant movement is slow but real.

q.t: Pot B has excess standing water. Why don't its seeds germinate?
o: Water drives out the air from soil spaces
q.e: The seeds drown despite plenty of water.

q.t: Why is Pot B 'the clever one'?
o: It has more water than D yet fails, showing air matters
q.e: Too much water excludes air.

q.t: Why do air spaces in soil matter?
o: Seeds use the air and roots grow easily
q.e: Air between soil particles supports germination and root growth.

q.t: Seeds of Coleus and Petunia…
q.e: They are exceptions; covering them stops sprouting.

q.t: Seeds of Calendula and Zinnia…
o: Need darkness and must be well covered
q.e: Another exception to the general rule.

q.t: How does Drosera trap insects?
o: Sticky hairs move inward around the insect
It closes like a box instantly
q.e: Saucer-shaped leaves with sticky-tipped hairs.

q.t: Which experiment pot germinates AND is the 'complete' set-up?
q.e: D has water, air and light.

q.t: Which shows respiration in animals?
q.e: Respiration involves air going in and out.

q.t: Why is reproduction necessary?
q.e: Without it, a kind of living thing would die out.

q.t: A robot can move and respond to sound. Is it living?
o: No — it can't grow, reproduce or respire
q.e: It doesn't show all the characteristics.

q.t: In the four-pot experiment, why change only one condition per pot?
o: So any difference is due to that condition
q.e: Otherwise you can't tell which condition caused the result.

q.t: Which pots DON'T germinate?
q.e: A lacks water, B lacks air.

q.t: A gardener overwaters seeds in a pot with no drainage. Likely result?
q.e: Standing water excludes air, like Pot B.

q.t: Why does water help germination?
o: Softens seed coat and lets embryo develop
q.e: Water enables the processes of growth.

q.t: A stone is still, doesn't grow, eat or reproduce. It is…
q.e: It never showed life characteristics — non-living, not dead.

q.t: A dried leaf on the ground is…
q.e: It once showed life characteristics.

q.t: Pulling your hand away from a hot cup is…
q.e: The heat is the stimulus.

q.t: Plants differ from animals in nutrition because they…
q.e: Animals eat food; plants make it (Drosera also traps insects).

q.t: How many characteristics must a living being show?
q.e: No single characteristic is enough.

q.t: A seed kept in a dry jar for years doesn't sprout. Is it dead?
o: Not necessarily — it lacks water and air to germinate
q.e: Given the right water and air, many seeds sprout.
